MAJAZ:v1p14/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p14/r6.claim: Here على means ‘from’: they take full measure from the people.
MAJAZ:v1p14/r6.anchor: وقال: «إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون» (83/ 2) معناه: من الناس

BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r1.claim: The relative clause explains how the cheaters shortchange others and why they merit condemnation: when receiving measured goods in a purchase, they take the full amount and more.
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r1.anchor: صفة كاشفة للمطففين شارحة لكيفية تطفيفهم الذي استحقوا به الذم

BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r2.claim: Iktiāl means taking goods by measure, like ittizān means taking by weight; ‘upon the people’ can imply dominance or seizure, not merely receiving one’s due.
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r2.anchor: أي من الناس مكيلهم بحكم الشراء ونحوه والاكتيال الأخذ بالكيل

BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r3.claim: Their istīfā’ is not fair receipt of an exact right but taking an abundant amount through any available trick, including packing measures, shaking them, and stealing from their rims and scale tongues.
BURSEVI:v10p282#2/r3.anchor: بل مجرد الأخذ الوافي الوافر حسبما أرادوا بأي وجه يتيسر من وجوه الحيل

QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.claim: Beyond literal cheating in measures, the verses concern cheating on the true scale of justice, where character and deeds are measured.
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.anchor: يمكن أن يحمل بعد الظاهر على التطفيف في الميزان الحقيقي الذي هو العدل، والموزونات به هي الأخلاق والأعمال

QASHANI:83:1-5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:83:1-5/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:83:1-5/r2.claim: Such people overstate their own intellectual and practical virtues in relation to others from vanity and pride.
QASHANI:83:1-5/r2.anchor: يستكثرونها ويزيدون على حقوقهم في إظهار الفضائل العلمية والعملية أكثر مما لهم عجبا وتكبرا

FARRA:v3p245#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p245#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p245#2/r4.claim: اكتالوا على الناس means “took from people”; على and من alternate because the amount is owed to them, though the prepositions emphasize different sides of the transaction.
FARRA:v3p245#2/r4.anchor: وهما تعتقبان: على ومن- في هذا الموضع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r1.claim: Iktālū ʿalā al-nās means they bought measured goods from people; the measured object is omitted because the verb makes it understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r1.anchor: فمعنى : { اكتالوا على الناس } اشتروا من الناس ما يباع بالكيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r5.claim: The buyers' side mentions measuring alone because they usually bought produce by measure and paid in weighed coin; sellers use both measure and weight, revealing that the cheating was merchants' practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p191/r5.anchor: فلذلك اقتصر في ابتياعهم من الجالبين على الاكتيال نظرا إلى الغالب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r1.claim: Yastawfūn answers “when”: istīfāʾ means taking the full amount, with the added letters intensifying the action.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r1.anchor: والاستيفاء أخذ الشيء وافيا ، فالسين والتاء فيه للمبالغة في الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r3.claim: The passage warns Muslims against widespread short-measure practices in early Medina and condemns the polytheists of Medina and Mecca.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية تحذير للمسلمين من التساهل في التطفيف إذ وجوده فاشيا في المدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r4.claim: Short measure combines injustice, theft, and meanness, traits the Arabs disdained separately yet practiced together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r4.anchor: أن التطفيف يجمع ظلما واختلاسا ولؤما

NAHHAS:v5p173/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p173/r6.claim: الذين may be a genitive adjective to المطففين or accusative as a condemnation; the latter better suits the verse.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r6.anchor: الذين في موضع خفض نعت للمطففين أو نصب على الذم وهو أولى بالآية

NAHHAS:v5p173/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p173/r7.claim: اكتال عليه means taking what is owed from him, while اكتال منه means receiving the full measure from him; the expressions are not synonymous.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r8.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r8.claim: اكتالوا على الناس means taking measure from customers, while كالوهم means measuring for them; dropping the preposition makes the verb take an object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r8.anchor: واكتالوا على الناس معناه: قبضوا منهم وكالوهم معناه: قبضوهم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r9.speaker: أبو زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r9.claim: Abu Zayd's verse illustrates the construction with an omitted prepositional complement.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r1.speaker: المفسرون واللغويون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r1.claim: Interpreters and linguists take “ʿalā al-nās” as “from the people,” with ʿalā functioning like min.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r1.anchor: على الناس أي من الناس ف على بمعنى من في قول المفسرين واللغويين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains that “measuring against you” can mean taking the amount owed from you, while “measuring from you” means receiving full measure from you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r2.anchor: قال الفراء على و من يعتقبان في هذا الموضع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says buyers who measure or weigh from others take the full amount; weighing is left implicit because goods are bought and sold by either measure or weight, and one indicates the other.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل وكذلك إذا اتزنوا ولم يذكر إذا اتزنوا

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5.speaker: عامة القراء
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5.claim: The common reading joins “they measure for them” as a transitive construction, with “them” as the object; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar instead pauses after “they measure” and starts “they are defrauders” with “they” as subject, a reading attributed to Ḥamzah.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5.anchor: قراءة العامة: (كالوهم أو وزنوهم) متصلا بغير ألف، ولا وقف بين (كالوا)، وبين (هم).

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6.claim: The author prefers the joined reading because the written form lacks an alif, Arabic says “I measured your due” meaning “for you,” and the readers unanimously use it.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6.anchor: والأوجه الأول لوجوه: أحدها: أنهم كتبوها بغير ألف

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.claim: Ṭafīf means tiny or insignificant; a mutaffif reduces another person's proper measure or weight, whether by a small shortfall or a subtle theft.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.anchor: الطفيف: الشيء التفه القليل، والمطفف: المقلل حق صاحبه بنقصانه

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.claim: One explanation names the act for the tiny amount missing from the rightful measure.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.anchor: وقيل: لأن ما ينقص منه طفيف قليل

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.claim: Another view calls the act a secret theft of a small amount.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.anchor: وقيل: التطفيف: أن يسرق الشيء اليسير في خفية

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.claim: Related usage describes an underfilled vessel and says all descendants of Adam are close to a full measure.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.anchor: وإناء طفان إذا لم يكن ملآن، ومنه: بنو آدم كلهم طف الصاع

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.claim: No one has superiority over another except through piety.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.anchor: فليس لأحد على أحد فضل إلا بالتقوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r11.claim: Using ala where min might be expected signals that their taking from people harms and oppresses them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r11.anchor: لما كان اكتيالهم من الناس اكتيالا يضرهم ويتحامل فيه عليهم : أبدل ( على ) مكان ( من ) للدلالة على ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r12.claim: Alternatively, ala attaches to yastawfun, with the object fronted to stress that they take full measure from others in particular while taking their own in full.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق ( على ) بيستوفون ، ويقدم المفعول على الفعل لإفادة الخصوصية ، أي : يستوفون على الناس خاصة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r13.speaker: الفراء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r13.claim: Al-Farra says min and ala alternate here: iktaltu alayka means I took what was due from you, while iktaltu minka means I received it from you.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r13.anchor: وقال الفراء ( من ) و ( على ) يعتقبان في هذا الموضع ، لأنه حق عليه ؛ فإذا قال اكتلت عليك ، فكأنه قال : أخذت ما عليك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r11.claim: On acquiring measure from people, على means من; the cheater takes more than he is owed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r11.anchor: أي من الناس , ويريد بالاستيفاء الزيادة على ما استحق

MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2.claim: A report about the pre-Islamic market says buyers received extra measure while sellers gave short measure, using two measures and two scales and shifting between them.
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2.anchor: وكان بسوق الجاهلية لهم كيلين وميزانين معلومة لا يعاب عليهم فيها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r1.claim: They demand complete measure when taking from people; على instead of من indicates that taking from people burdens and disadvantages them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r1.anchor: ﴿ الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون ﴾ أى إذا أخذوا بالكيل من الناس يأخذون حقوقهم وافية تامة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r2.claim: The phrase may attach على to يستوفون, putting the object first to restrict their full measure to other people; al-Farrāʾ says من and على alternate here because the debt is owed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق على يستوفون ويقدم المفعول على الفعل لافادة الاختصاص

NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r3.speaker: الفراء
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats من and على as interchangeable here: taking from a person means collecting what is owed by that person.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#12/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء من وعلى يعتقبان فى هذا الموضع لأنه حق عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r1.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r1.claim: Al-Farra says ʿalā means “from”: buyers measuring from people insist on full measure.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: أي من الناس يقال: اكتلت منك: أي استوفيت منك

QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they take extra for themselves but shortchange others, refusing people what they would refuse themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أي إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.claim: A Prophetic warning pairs five wrongs with consequences: broken covenants bring enemies, rejecting God's law poverty, immorality plague, short measure drought, and withholding alms the loss of rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.anchor: خمس بخمس: ما نقض قوم العهد إلا سلط الله عليهم عدوهم

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits the warning by gist, and Malik also relates it from Ibn ʿUmar.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.anchor: خرجه أبو بكر البزار بمعناه، ومالك بن أنس أيضا من حديث ابن عمر.

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.speaker: مالك بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.claim: Malik ibn Dinar tells of a dying neighbor who used two measures and saw them grow into mountains of fire when struck together.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: دخلت على جار لي قد نزل به الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.claim: ʿIkrimah swears every measurer or weigher is destined for Hell, even when asked whether this applies to his son.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: أشهد على كل كيال أو وزان أنه في النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.claim: Al-Asmaʿi quotes a Bedouin saying manliness cannot reside in measure rims or scale tongues; it is also related from ʿAli.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.anchor: قال الأصمعي: وسمعت أعرابية تقول: لا تلتمس المروءة ممن مروءته

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.speaker: عبد خير
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.claim: ʿAbd Khayr says ʿAli overturned a scale that gave excess saffron, ordering accurate weight first and voluntary excess afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.anchor: وقال عبد خير: مر علي رضي الله عنه على رجل وهو يزن الزعفران وقد أرجح

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.claim: Nafiʿ says Ibn ʿUmar warned short-measurers will stand in sweat up to half their ears.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.anchor: وقال نافع: كان ابن عمر يمر بالبائع فيقول: اتق الله وأوف الكيل والوزن

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.claim: Abu Hurayrah says Medina's deputy recited this surah at dawn; he prayed against a trader who bought with full measure but sold short.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.anchor: وقرأ في الركعة الثانية «ويل للمطففين» قال أبو هريرة: فأقول في صلاتي

RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r6.claim: The preposition ʿalā in “they take from people” may signal harm and pressure imposed on them.
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r6.anchor: لما كان اكتيالهم من الناس اكتيالا فيه إضرار بهم وتحامل عليهم ، أقيم على مقام من

RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r7.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says min and ʿalā alternate here because the amount is owed: taking from someone is taking what is due against him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r7.anchor: قال الفراء : المراد اكتالوا من الناس

SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r1.claim: The phrase على الناس can attach to اكتالوا; على and من alternate in this usage, and al-Farrāʾ distinguishes taking full measure from taking what is owed. The author calls this first analysis clearer.
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه متعلق ب " اكتالوا " و " على " و " من " تعتقبان هنا. قال الفراء

SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r2.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says اكتلت على الناس means taking full measure from them, while اكتلت منهم means taking what they owe.
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: " يقال: اكتلت على الناس: استوفيت منهم، واكتلت منهم: أخذت ما عليهم "

SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r3.claim: Another analysis takes على as equivalent to من, as in the interchangeable expressions اكتلت عليه and اكتلت منه.
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r3.anchor: وقيل: " على " بمعنى " من ". يقال: اكتلت عليه ومنه، بمعنى

SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains على in place of من as signaling that their taking full measure burdens and harms other people.
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " لما كان اكتيالهم اكتيالا يضرهم ويتحامل فيه عليهم أبدل " على " مكان " من "

SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also attaches على الناس to يستوفون: fronting it restricts their full measure to other people, while they secure it for themselves; al-Samīn calls this good.
SAMIN-DURR:83:2/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تتعلق ب " يستوفون " ، وقدم المفعول على الفعل لإفادة الخصوصية، أي: يستوفون على الناس خاصة

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī describes wayl as a valley of Hell’s pus for those who shortchange people in measures and weights, withholding their due full amount; mutaffif comes from something slight or scant.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.anchor: والمطفف: المقلل حق صاحب الحق عما له من الوفاء والتمام في كيل أو وزن؛

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r2.claim: The expression people are equal like the taff of a measure means they are nearly level with a container that is almost, but not quite, full.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r2.anchor: هم سواء كطف الصاع، يعني بذلك: كقرب الممتلئ منه ناقص عن الملء

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r3.claim: When told Medina’s people fulfill measures, ʿAbd Allāh answers that they should, since God warned the fraudulent through the verse about standing before the Lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: قال له رجل: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، إن أهل المدينة ليوفون الكيل، قال: وما يمنعهم من أن يوفوا الكيل،

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.claim: ʿIkrima swears that every measurer and weigher is in the Fire: none gives the same measure or weight that they themselves demand.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: أشهد أن كل كيال ووزان في النار،

TAB-FULL:v24p186/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes ʿalā and min as interchangeable when people take their full due, and parses hum in the next clause as the object pronoun for those being shortchanged.
TAB-FULL:v24p186/r1.anchor: ومن وجه الكلام إلى هذا المعنى، جعل الوقف على هم، وجعل هم في موضع نصب.

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r6.claim: When they measure from others, they demand the full measure; likewise, when they buy by weight, they demand full weight.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r6.anchor: إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل وكذلك إذا اتزنوا استوفوا الوزن

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r7.claim: The verse does not separately mention their weighing when buying because buying and selling involve goods measured or weighed.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r7.anchor: والوزن بهما الشراء والبيع فيما يكال ويوزن.

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.claim: The sura opens by warning those who cheat in measure and weight that they will be resurrected for judgment on the Great Day, then describes the fates of wicked and righteous; context suggests the opening was revealed in Medina.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.anchor: تفتتح السورة بوعيد أهل التطفيف في الكيل والوزن وتنذرهم بأنهم مبعوثون للجزاء في يوم عظيم وهو يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r3.claim: Iktiyal means taking measured goods from people, with على signaling harm; Hijazi usage says kaalahu or wazanahu, which is the Qur'anic form, while other Arabs use kaala lahu or wazana lahu.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r3.anchor: من الناس الأخذ منهم بالكيل، وتعديته بعلى لإفادة معنى الضرر، والكيل إعطاؤهم بالمكيال يقال كاله طعامه ووزنه

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r4.claim: They take their full due when buying but reduce what they give when selling, thereby making others lose.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r4.anchor: والاستيفاء أخذ الحق تاما كاملا، والإخسار الإيقاع في الخسارة. والمعنى الذين إذا أخذوا من الناس بالكيل يأخذون حقهم تاما كاملا،

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r5.claim: Both verses condemn one wrong: they insist on rights for themselves but deny others equal reciprocal rights, corrupting a society built on balanced claims.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r5.anchor: الآيتين جميعا ذم واحد وهو أنهم يراعون الحق لأنفسهم ولا يراعونه لغيرهم وبعبارة أخرى لا يراعون لغيرهم من الحق مثل

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r6.claim: One explanation says only buying by measure is mentioned because dealers commonly bought bulk grain and resold small amounts, usually by measure; the author finds this weak.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r6.anchor: قيل لأن المطففين كانوا باعة وهم كانوا في الأغلب يشترون الكثير من الحبوب والبقول ونحوهما من الأمتعة ثم يكسبون بها

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r7.claim: Another says weighing need not be mentioned when buying because weight and measure jointly indicate buying and selling; the author says the reasoning also applies to measures and is arbitrary.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r7.anchor: وقيل لم يذكر الاتزان لأن الكيل والوزن بهما البيع والشراء فذكر أحدهما يدل على الآخر. وفيه أن ما ذكر في

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r8.claim: A third explanation says the original cheats bought only by measure but sold by measure and weight; the author calls this an unsupported claim, and finds the other explanations weak too.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r8.anchor: وقيل الآيتان تحاكيان ما كان عليه دأب الذين نزلت فيهم السورة فقد كانوا يشترون بالاكتيال فقط ويبيعون بالكيل والوزن جميعا،

TABRISI:83:1-3/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:83:1-3/r16.claim: When measuring what people owe them, they take the full amount; measuring is named while weighing is implied as its counterpart in trade.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r16.anchor: أي إذا كالوا ما على الناس ليأخذوه لأنفسهم

THALABI:v10p149#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p149#3/r3.claim: When buyers take measure from people, على and من are interchangeable in this context.
THALABI:v10p149#3/r3.anchor: الذين إذا اكتالوا أخذوا على الناس أي منهم، وعلى ومن تتعاقبان في هذا الموضع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r1.claim: Iktiyāl means taking by measure, just as ittizān is taking by weight.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r1.anchor: الاكتيال: الأخذ بالكيل كالاتزان: الأخذ بالوزن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the phrase means they take from people; ʿalā and min alternate here because the buyer takes what is owed to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: يريد اكتالوا من الناس. و"على"، و"من" في هذا الموضع تعتقبان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says they demand full measure from people; the mention of measuring suffices for both measuring and weighing because either can stand for buying and selling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r3.anchor: أبو إسحاق: المعنى: إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل، ولم يذكر اتزنوا؛ لأن الكيل والوزن بهما (¬5) الشراء والبيع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r4.claim: The commentators mean that such people take full measure and weight when buying for themselves but reduce it when selling or weighing for others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p309#2/r4.anchor: المفسرون (¬2): يعني الذين إذا اشتروا لأنفسهم استوفوا في الكيل والوزن، وإذا باعوا أو وزنوا لغيرهم نقصوا

ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.claim: Authentic traditions cited by Tabari, Baghawi, and Ibn Kathir place at least the first four verses shortly after the Prophet's arrival in Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.anchor: However, a number of authentic Traditions make it clear that at least the first four verses were

ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.claim: The condemned demand full measure when receiving from others but give less than their due when measuring or weighing what they owe.
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.anchor: give less than what is due! [1]

ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.claim: The warning extends beyond commerce to every practical and moral social relation, including each person's rights, obligations, and possessions.
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.anchor: does not, of course, refer only to commercial dealings but touches upon every aspect of social relations, both practical and moral

ELMALILI:83:2-3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:2-3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:2-3/r1.claim: The wording says buyers take full measure for themselves against people; using 'against' rather than 'from' signals acting to people's detriment, asserting power and insisting on full value.
ELMALILI:83:2-3/r1.anchor: Burada ifadenin zâhiri مِنَ النَّاس “nâstan” denilmekti, عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ buyurulması kendi lehlerine olarak nâsın aleyhine istîlâ ve tecavüz suretiyle ölçtüklerine işaret içindir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Muṭaffifīn supplements al-Infiṭār, sharing its theme and elaborating the division of righteous and defiant people at its end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.anchor: This sūrah  is a supplement to S ūrah al-Infi ṭār

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.claim: Al-Infiṭār reasons from God’s attributes displayed in the human body, while this sūrah reasons from the moral nature God gave people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.anchor: attributes of God that are prominent in man’s physical being

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.claim: Human nature loves justice and good and dislikes injustice and evil; this moral distinction shows that the Creator differentiates the just from the unjust rather than treating them alike.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.anchor: by his very nature man likes justice and what is good

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.claim: People commit injustice when other motives overpower their nature, as shown by the dishonest trader who protests when others cheat him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.anchor: the very person who is dishonest in weighing to others cries out with anguish if others are dishonest with him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly uses this reasoning for the Day of Judgement; the author points to his discussion of 75:14–15.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.anchor: readers can take a look at what I have written under the following verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.claim: Verses 1–6 censure people who demand fair treatment while cheating others; their conduct shows they do not expect to be raised before their Lord for judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.anchor: An expression of regret on people who want

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.claim: Taṭfīf means giving short measure or weight.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.anchor: The word !ْ#ْﺗﻄﻔﻴﻒ refers to measuring and weighing less

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r3.claim: The verse contrasts people who insist on full measure from others with their own dishonesty toward others, exposing a moral inconsistency rather than merely naming a trading practice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r3.anchor: a person is very sensitive and vigilant that others should weigh and measure correctly for him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r1.claim: Such a cheater knows justice requires the same honesty for both sides; he violates his own nature from selfishness, committing open and mean injustice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r1.anchor: he in fact goes against his own nature purely being overwhelmed with selfishness

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r2.claim: God placed in people a moral barometer that makes them dislike oppression and like justice; when they oppress, desire or emotion overwhelms their ability to keep balance, not their ability to recognize right and wrong.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r2.anchor: The real reason, as pointed out above, is because he is so overcome by some desire or emotion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r3.claim: Thieves, murderers, and adulterers would not want the same harm done to their own households, and even impartially acknowledge that society should protect life, wealth, and integrity for everyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r3.anchor: Only those people should be members of a society who protect the life, wealth and integrity of others

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.claim: This nature shows that people distinguish good from evil and expect different treatment; God must therefore judge righteous and wrongdoers, and the deniers resist because they wish to evade that outcome.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.anchor: An obvious corollary of this is that the Almighty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.speaker: exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.claim: Exegetes report that dishonest measuring among the Anṣār occasioned revelation of this verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.anchor: While explaining this verse, our exegetes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.claim: The author challenges that report’s setting: the sūrah is Meccan, and dishonest trade was at least as plausible among the Meccan traders as among the agricultural Anṣār.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.claim: Even if the Anṣār had the practice, it was no more prevalent than among the Meccans, who were traders, while the Anṣār’s profession was agriculture; the verse’s main point is innate recognition of justice, which implies judgement and accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.anchor: In fact, there was a much greater chance

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.claim: Taffif is reduction, from something tiny and insignificant; a mutaffif cheats by an inconspicuous small amount in weight or measure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.anchor: التطفيف النقصان وأصله من الطفيف وهو النزل الحقير والمطفف الآخذ في وزن أو كيل طفيفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10.claim: When they measure for others, they collect what is due to themselves; when they measure or weigh for others, they make the recipients take less.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10.anchor: إذا اكتالوا على الناس: قبضوا لهم، وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم، أقبضوهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r1.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r1.claim: He says من and على alternate: measuring from someone means collecting one's due from them, while measuring on them means taking what they owe; Abu Hayyan prefers على as the direct complement of اكتالوا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r1.anchor: وقال الفراء: من وعلى يعتقبان هنا، اكتلت على الناس، واكتلت من الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r2.claim: He says على signals burdensome, harmful measuring, or it may attach to يستوفون to emphasize they take full measure from others while doing so for themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لما كان اكتيالهم من الناس اكتيالا يضرهم ويتحامل فيه عليهم، أبدل على مكان من

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r3.claim: He says the apparent parsing attaches على to اكتالوا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن على متعلق باكتالوا كما قررنا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r1.claim: The clause can define which defrauders are meant or describe their characteristic conduct: when taking from people in a sale, they demand a full, generous measure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r1.anchor: صفة مخصصة للمطففين الذين نزلت فيهم الآية أو صفة كاشفة لحالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r2.claim: One account says “against people” reflects the grasping force of taking over; another says it marks harm to people, since they obtain full measure by compaction, shaking, and similar tricks.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r2.anchor: لتضمين الاكتيال معنى الاستيلاء أو للإشارة إلى أنه اكتيال مضر للناس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ says min and ʿala interchange here: they take in full what is owed to them by others.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r3.anchor: فعن الفراء أن من وعلى يعتقبان في هذا الموضع فيقال اكتلت عليه أي أخذت ما عليه كيلا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r4.claim: Alusi reports objections: this gloss misses ordinary purchases from people to whom no debt is owed, and “taking in full” ordinarily means receiving one's due, so it alone does not explain the condemnation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r4.anchor: مع اقتضائه لعدم شمول لاكتيالهم قبل أن يكون لهم على الناس شيء بطريق الشراء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r5.claim: Alusi answers that the paired conduct condemns them as in saying someone takes his due fully but gives others theirs short; this combination is blameworthy even if full receipt alone is proper.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r5.anchor: قلنا مدار الذم ما تضمنه مجموع المتعاطفين والكلام كقولك فلان يأخذ حقه من الناس تاما ويعطيهم حقهم ناقصا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r6.claim: Since a person's purchase from another usually concerns a due acquired through trade, al-Farraʾ may be describing the common case; the author invites consideration.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r6.anchor: ثم يقال إن الأغلب في اكتيال الشخص من شخص كون المكيل حقا له بوجه من الوجوه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r7.claim: A proposed focus reading takes “against people” with “they take in full,” meaning they do so only against others, not themselves; critics say taking fully from oneself is not a plausible contrast.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r7.anchor: وجوز على أن تكون على متعلقة بيستوفون ويكون تقديمها على الفعل لأفادة الخصوصية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r8.claim: Its defenders paraphrase the focus as harming others but not themselves, since they take extra from buyers while taking less when selling; Alusi remains unconvinced.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68#2/r8.anchor: وأجيب بأن المراد بالاستيفاء المعدي بعلى على ذلك الإضرار فكأنه قيل إذا اكتالوا يضرون الناس خاصة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r1.claim: The wording means when they take a measure from people; min and ʿala can alternate in this construction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r1.anchor: وأراد إذا اكتالوا من الناس أي أخذوا منهم و"من" و"على" متعاقبان.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r2.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says that when they buy for themselves, they take full measure and weight from others.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: المعنى إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل [الوزن]

BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r4.claim: Cheaters take their dues from people in full; ʿalā instead of min marks a due owed by others or oppressive measuring against them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r4.anchor: أي إذا اكتالوا من الناس حقوقهم يأخذونها وافية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r8.claim: The preposition ʿalā portrays the fraudsters as acting from a position of superiority over customers; they demand full or more than full measure for themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r8.anchor: مستعلين أو متحاملين { على الناس } أي خاصة بمشاهدتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r9.claim: The expression may signal that they exploit anyone, especially a weak person; iktāl can take either min or ʿalā, while yastawfūn means they obtain complete measure eagerly and emphatically.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r9.anchor: وهذا الفعل يتعدى بمن وعلى , يقال : اكتال من الرجل وعليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r10.claim: The verse omits ‘weigh’ when describing their own purchases because weighing offers less opportunity for deliberate extra fullness than measuring; shortchanging, however, is possible in both.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r10.anchor: فكأنه ذكر ( اكتالوا ) ولم يذكر ( اتزنوا ) لأنه لا يتأتى في الوزن

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p219/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p219/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p219/r6.claim: The phrase إذا اكتالوا على الناس is glossed “from the people,” illustrating على in place of من.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p219/r6.anchor: الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون [المطففين: 2] . أي من الناس

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p219/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p219/r7.speaker: صخر الغي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p219/r7.claim: Ṣakhr al-Ghayy’s على أقطارها is glossed من أقطارها, an example of على meaning من.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p219/r7.anchor:
وقال صخر الغي :
متى ما تنكروها تعرفوها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p300#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p300#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p300#3/r1.claim: In إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون, على is glossed مع الناس (“with the people”).
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p300#3/r1.anchor: إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون (2) [المطففين: 2] ، أي مع الناس

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p300#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p300#3/r2.speaker: صخر الغي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p300#3/r2.claim: The poet’s على أقطارها is glossed من أقطارها, showing على used with the sense من.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p300#3/r2.anchor:
وقال صخر الغي :
متى ما تنكروها تعرفوها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r1.claim: The ordinary expression is اكتال من, while اكتال على in 83:2 signals that the defrauders dominate and impose themselves on people rather than measure from them normally.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p124/r1.anchor: في الأصل يقال اكتال من ولا يقال اكتال على

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p572/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p572/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p572/r3.claim: Using ʿalā instead of the usual min portrays the defrauders as domineering over people when taking measure.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p572/r3.anchor: وقد عدّى فعل اكتال في هذه الآية بحرف على للدلالة على التسلط

BURHAN:v3p165/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p165/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p165/r1.claim: The author rejects the preceding analysis of كالوهم and وزنوهم on two grounds: the spelling lacks the alif expected by that reading, and الناس shows that the pronoun refers to the people; thus they take full measure from people but give people short measure.
BURHAN:v3p165/r1.anchor: والثاني أن تقدم ذكر الناس يدل على أن الضمير راجع إليهم

BURHAN:v3p342/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p342/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p342/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the verb carries the sense of تحاملوا, so it takes على although its usual complement is introduced by من.
BURHAN:v3p342/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري ضمن معنى تحاملوا فعداه ب على والأصل فيه من

BURHAN:v3p342/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p342/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p342/r2.claim: Transitivity usually follows the implied, omitted meaning rather than the expressed word; examples take الرفث as الإفضاء and drinking by a spring as being quenched by it.
BURHAN:v3p342/r2.anchor: الأكثر أن يراعى في التعدية ما ضمن منه وهو المحذوف لا المذكور

BURHAN:v3p342/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p342/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v3p342/r5.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr gives another definition of تضمين: a meaning conveyed without naming it, arising either from a word's form or from a phrase's semantic requirements.
BURHAN:v3p342/r5.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر في كتاب إعجاز القرآن 3 هو حصول معنى فيه من غير ذكره له باسم أو صفه 4 هي عبارة عنه

BURHAN:v3p342/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p342/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v3p342/r6.claim: One kind of implication follows from morphology: معلوم necessarily implies an عالم.
BURHAN:v3p342/r6.anchor: أحدهما ما يفهم من البنية كقولك معلوم فإنه يوجب أنه لا بد من عالم

BURHAN:v3p342/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p342/r7.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v3p342/r7.claim: A second kind follows from the meaning of an expression, which cannot be realized without the implied complement: ضارب entails مضروب.
BURHAN:v3p342/r7.anchor: والثاني من معنى العبارة من حيث لا يصح إلابه 4 كالصفة فضارب يدل على مضروب

BURHAN:v3p342/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p342/r8.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v3p342/r8.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr calls all تضمين concise expression and treats the basmala as teaching people to begin acts in God's name for reverence or blessing.
BURHAN:v3p342/r8.anchor: قال والتضمين كله إيجاز قال وذكر أن ﴿ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ﴾ من باب التضمين
